subject: RegenHealth: perf targets, concurrency & dedicated capacity pilot
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@regenhealth.com>, Meera Singh <meera@regenhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RegenHealth discovery — perf targets & HW check

Hi Sam / Meera — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a dedicated-capacity pilot that validates your SLOs.

Summary (asks you confirmed):
- P95 latency target: <= 120 ms for streaming responses (token-by-token).
- Throughput: baseline 200 req/s, peak bursts up to 350 req/s for short windows.
- Concurrency: steady-state ~30 concurrent streams, peak ~55.
- Typical prompt/response length: ~380 input tokens / ~120 output tokens.
- Model family: you indicated preference for an LLM in the 13B–34B range; open to quantized variants.

Pilot objectives
- Verify achievable p95 streaming latency at your peak concurrency and throughput under realistic traffic patterns.
- Produce reserved-throughput guidance (per-GPU) and an ops runbook for autoscaling + fallback.
- Provide an estimated cost delta across GPU options (H100 / A10G / L40S) for the expected workload.

Hardware shortlist (initial hypothesis)
- H100 (single-GPU and NVLINK pair) — best-case latency for streaming with large KV caches.
- A10G — cost-efficient option for steady throughput, slightly higher p95 expected under high concurrency.
- L40S — good for batch-heavy rerank/embedding jobs, not first choice for low-latency streaming.

Immediate asks from us to run a valid baseline:
1) Share a sample of representative payloads (we can accept anonymized input/response pairs). I attached a template: regen_payload_sample.json (small stub).
2) Confirm whether encryption keys must be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) during the pilot.
3) If available, a short CSV of minute-by-minute request rates for a recent 24–72 hour window helps us size reserved throughput.

Proposed timeline
- Today–Thu: exchange payload + traffic CSV + preliminary SOW.
- Week of Jun 21: baseline perf run on our dedicated staging cluster (H100 + A10G nodes), 48–72h sustained window.
- Week of Jun 28: present results and recommended reserved throughput + ops runbook.

Next step: are you able to share the traffic CSV and confirm KMS preference by EOD tomorrow? Happy to set a 30-minute kickoff to align the pilot test matrix.

Thanks —
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: regen_payload_sample.json (attachment stub)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@regenhealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: Meera Singh <meera@regenhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RegenHealth discovery — perf targets & HW check

Maya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items below and answering your asks:

- We can confirm p95 <= 120ms is our customer-facing SLO for streaming replies. If you can show that at 95% of peak (so ~330 req/s sustained for short windows) that will be compelling.
- Payload profile: average prompt length is ~380 tokens, average response ~120 tokens. We have rare long tails but they’re <2% of traffic.
- Concurrency: steady 30, spikes to 55 during morning syncs.
- KMS: we require customer-managed keys for production, but for the pilot we can use Redwood-managed keys if necessary (we prefer to test with our KMS if it’s supported).

I attached a minute-level sample of traffic for a recent 48-hour window (production_traffic_pattern.csv). We’ve redacted PII.

Pilot: we’re ok with Redwood running the baseline on H100 + A10G; please include a cost estimate for both so we can compare.

Two small asks from our side:
1) We need to confirm that model version pinning will be supported during canary/rollouts.
2) We will need SOC2 evidence and a short checklist of what telemetry/logs you’ll expose for the pilot (request IDs, token-level latency, KV cache hit rate).

Sam
Sam Patel
Director of Platform Engineering, RegenHealth
sam.patel@regenhealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0133

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RegenHealth discovery — perf targets & HW check

Thanks — dug into the CSV Sam sent and sketched a test matrix and preliminary hw guidance. Key points below; I attached a short workbook with rough numbers (latency_benchmark_v1.xlsx).

Test matrix (baseline run)
- Models: quantized 13B (nf4/int8) and 34B (nf4) — run both to compare p95 and throughput.
- Nodes: standalone H100 (1x), H100 NVLINK pair (2x), A10G (1x), and L40S (1x) run as separate suites.
- Window: 72 hours with two 2-hour peak windows replayed at 1x and 1.5x to stress concurrency.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 streaming latency, tokens/sec sustained, KV cache hit %, tail-burst recovery time.

Prelim observations from the sample traffic
- Sustained burst shapes suggest reserved throughput should be provisioned per-queue rather than per-GPU instance; we’ll supply a mapping (requests/sec -> GPUs).
- For your token sizes, an H100 single GPU for quantized 13B should comfortably deliver p95 ~90–110ms at 30–40 concurrent streams, and hit ~260–320 req/s equivalent depending on batching aggressiveness and KV cache hits.
- A10G looks ~20–35% slower on p95 under the same concurrency but is ~40% lower cost per-hour.

Reserved throughput guidance (rough)
- H100 (13B quantized): reserve 300 req/s per 1–2 GPU pool (depends on autoscale buckets).
- A10G (13B quantized): reserve 200 req/s per GPU.
- L40S: not recommended as primary for streaming; better as mixed batch worker.

Ops notes
- Continuous batching + small batching window (5–10ms) will help maintain throughput without blowing up p95 for short prompts.
- KV cache strategy: pin hot prefixes to cache to lower overall token compute. We’ll run a KV hit-rate sweep during the pilot.

Next steps I’ll own: assemble an exact per-GPU perf run commandset, target images/configs for 13B/34B quantized runs, and a cost delta spreadsheet. Can schedule the baseline run once we have the final sample payload + KMS preference.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam / Meera — thanks for the quick confirmations and the CSV. Proposed mutual action plan and kickoff details below. If this looks good I’ll send the pilot SOW (DocuSign) and book the baseline window.

Mutual action plan (pilot scope)
- You: provide final anonymized payloads + confirm KMS preference by Jun 20.
- Redwood: run 72h baseline across H100 (single & NVLINK), A10G, 13B quantized (nf4/int8) and 34B (nf4), produce a short runbook and reserved-throughput recommendation.
- Deliverables: perf report (p50/p95/p99), ops runbook, cost delta table, and a short SOC2 evidence bundle for pilot telemetry.

Kickoff: we propose Mon Jun 21 08:00–10:00 PT for the baseline run start. That gives us room to ingest payloads and validate configs on Jun 20.

DocuSign: I’ll send the pilot SOW via DocuSign after you confirm the KMS preference. DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/prepare/RGN-4921-pilot-sow

If you prefer a short 20-min alignment call tomorrow afternoon, I’m available 2–4pm PT.

Best,
